text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 1.9% today after hitting a three-week low two days ago, recovering some ground in a volatile week. The move appears tied to conflicting signals on geopolitical risk: while President Trump suggested the Iran conflict could end "fairly soon" and crude briefly dipped below $90, Secretary of State Rubio on the same day called Iranian demands "outrageous" and said negotiations remain unproductive, leaving the path to peace unclear. Oil refining margins depend heavily on stable crude prices, and this whipsaw between peace hopes and diplomatic pessimism creates uncertainty for refiners like this one.

The broader context is that U.S. refineries are running at a healthy 94.5% capacity with crude inventories elevated at 692 million barrels, so the company has room to capture margins if crude prices stabilize—but the two-week decline of 9.9% reflects genuine concern about where energy prices head if Middle East tensions truly ease.
